## Review verdict

| # | Finding | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Permission IA Drift on /admin** (crime_00001, agent_risk 0.59) | **Block merge** | Three different role tokens (`admin`, `manager`, `owner`) for the same destination across nav, guard, and docs. Authorization drift is silent: an agent fixing one site won't fix the others, and no test fails when access widens. Resolve before merge by picking a canonical token and routing every caller through one check. |
| 2 | **Command docs drift** (crime_00005, agent_risk 0.51) — docs reference `iaq teams / workspace / refresh`; bin advertises only `get, list` | **Warn** | Loud failure mode (`command not found`), not silent. An agent following the docs gets an immediate error and stops. Fix shape is mechanical (regen command docs from the bin, or codify in CI). Doesn't have to block merge but shouldn't ship without an issue/owner. |
| 3 | **Parallel destination** `/admin/billing-plans` ↔ `/billing-plans` (crime_00006, agent_risk 0.48) | **Warn** | Two routes with overlapping intent, no link between them, both currently orphaned (crimes 7 & 8). An agent updating one billing flow won't see the other — same trap as #1, but the blast radius is narrower (one feature) and the duplication is visible at the file-tree level. Demand a decision (merge / redirect / document the split) before either route gets wired into a journey. |

Everything else (orphans, alias drift, action label drift, missing AGENTS.md) is **warn-to-ignore** — real signal, not merge-blocking.

## Highest agent-risk: Permission IA Drift (0.59)

Numerically it tops the report, but the reason it deserves the verdict is structural, not the score:

1. **Three sources of truth, three different tokens.** `nav.ts` says `role=admin`, `routes/admin.ts` mixes `admin / manager / owner` in the guard itself, `docs/routes.md` describes a third shape. An agent asked to "add a new admin page" or "tighten admin access" will pattern-match *one* of these and silently diverge from the others.
2. **The failure mode is silent and security-adjacent.** Compare to crime_00005 (command drift) — that one fails loudly with `command not found`. A misaligned role check fails by letting the wrong person through; no test catches it because `test_gap` is 1.0.
3. **The fix shape ("centralise the permission check") is exactly the refactor agents half-do.** They'll add a helper, route two of three callers through it, and leave the third — re-creating the drift one layer deeper. That's why this needs human review before merge, not "agent, please clean this up."

The parallel destination (#3) is the same *shape* of risk — multiple surfaces for one concept — but with a narrower blast radius and a louder smell (two route files literally named the same thing). The command drift (#2) has a higher confidence score but a much more forgiving failure mode.
